zh.question: 开花植物怎样从一粒种子走到下一代，哪些步骤并不保证成功？
zh.observe: 先改变菜豆的水、空气和温度并翻动成长相册；再比较樱桃相容与不相容花粉；最后观察蒲公英风播或牛蒡接触、携带和落地。留意条件图：到达不是萌发，授粉不是已经受精。

academic.title: 萌发是有条件的重新生长
academic.body: 健康菜豆吸水后恢复代谢，胚根先伸出，胚轴把子叶抬起，之后真叶展开。水、氧气与适宜温度是本模型的条件；积水可能限制氧气供应。已经长出的结构不会因为改成缺水而变回种子，画面只暂停后续生长。早期使用种子储备，建立后的幼苗还需光、水和矿质养分，并经过足够生长才能达到生殖成熟。本页不模拟从幼苗长到开花，也不把菜豆换成樱桃。

academic.title: 授粉、受精与果实不是同一个事件
academic.body: 樱桃案例从成熟树上的花开始。蜜蜂把花粉带到柱头是授粉，花粉管随后沿花柱生长，才可能向胚珠输送精细胞并完成受精。相容案例还假定其他条件适宜；不相容案例让花粉管在花柱中受阻，种子和果实不会继续出现。通常受精后的胚珠发育成种子，子房形成果实，子房壁形成果皮；樱桃肉与硬核属于果皮，硬核本身不是种子。此教学分支不是对所有品种、授粉量和环境的产量预测。

academic.title: 传播之后还要跨过建立门槛
academic.body: 蒲公英比较展示带冠毛的小果实随风平移并沉降；牛蒡比较展示带钩总苞接触毛发后附着、随同移动、脱落与下落。它们不是樱桃后续变成的两种形态。模型保留传播体身份，但落地后不会自动生成幼苗：种子活力、休眠状态、环境与物种要求仍会影响萌发和建立。关系图是一条典型有性繁殖路线，不能覆盖无融合生殖、营养繁殖或所有无籽果实。

zh.misconception: 不是每粒种子落地都会发芽，也不是每朵授粉的花都会结出果实；蒲公英冠毛带走的是小果实，樱桃硬核里面才是种子。几个比较案例不是同一棵植物变换物种。
zh.boundary: 菜豆为健康种子的条件相册，低温或缺氧用暂停后续生长表示。樱桃有相容成功与不相容受阻两个示意案例，不计算实际结实概率。传播轨迹和所有阶段时长都未按实测标定，不计算风场或萌发率。各案例状态分别保存、切换暂停；时间回拖是回看，不是植物倒着生长。

narration.label: 先要有合适条件
narration.text: 一粒豆子里面藏着小小的新生命。水让它重新活跃起来，但一直泡在水里也不好，因为它还需要氧气。条件合适时，通常先看到小根。
narration.cue: 菜豆从起点开始，对比干燥、积水与湿润，恢复条件后观察根先伸出。

narration.label: 幼苗不是立刻开花
narration.text: 嫩芽向上伸，真叶展开了。它还要得到光、水和养分，继续长大，才可能开花。接下来，我们换到一株已经长大的樱桃树：这是另一个比较案例。
narration.cue: 保留菜豆真叶状态，指出成熟桥段未模拟，然后切到樱桃并强调物种不同。

narration.label: 花粉到了还不够
narration.text: 蜜蜂把花粉带到花心。合适的花粉管继续生长，才可能帮助完成受精。也有花粉到了却不成功的时候。樱桃形成后，硬核里面藏着种子。
narration.cue: 在同一樱桃剖面比较相容和不相容案例，指出受阻花粉管与没有果实的结果。

narration.label: 落地后再问一次
narration.text: 再看另外两种植物：蒲公英的小果实搭风，牛蒡的小钩搭上动物的毛。它们到了新地方，却不会自动长成小苗。让我们再问一次：这里有合适的水、空气和温度吗？
narration.cue: 观察风播落地与牛蒡接触携带后脱落，读条件图，再返回保留状态的菜豆对照。

en.question: How can a flowering plant reach its next generation, and which steps can fail?
en.observe: Change the bean’s water, air and temperature and scrub its growth album. Compare compatible and incompatible cherry pollen, then inspect dandelion dispersal or burdock contact, transport and landing. Watch the condition map: arrival is not germination, and pollination is not fertilization.

academic.title: Germination is conditional renewed growth
academic.body: A healthy common bean resumes metabolism after taking up water. Its radicle emerges, its hypocotyl lifts the cotyledons, and true leaves unfold. Water, oxygen and suitable temperature are the conditions represented here; flooding can limit oxygen supply. Changing to dry soil does not turn existing structures back into a seed: later growth pauses. Early growth uses stored reserves, while an established seedling needs light, water, mineral nutrients and sufficient growth to become reproductively mature. Seedling-to-flowering growth is not simulated, and the bean never becomes a cherry.

academic.title: Pollination, fertilization and fruit are different events
academic.body: The cherry comparison begins with a flower on a mature tree. Pollen arriving on the stigma is pollination. A pollen tube then grows through the style before sperm can reach an ovule and fertilization can occur. The compatible case assumes other conditions are suitable; incompatible pollen-tube growth is arrested and no seeds or fruit develop in that case. A fertilized ovule usually develops into a seed; the ovary becomes the fruit and its wall becomes the pericarp. Cherry flesh and stone are pericarp: the stone itself is not a seed. This teaching branch is not a yield prediction across cultivars, pollen quantities or environments.

academic.title: Dispersal still leaves an establishment hurdle
academic.body: The dandelion comparison shows a pappus-bearing small fruit settling while wind carries it sideways. Burdock’s hooked bracts first contact fur, then remain attached during transport before release and falling. These are different species, not later forms of a cherry. Each dispersal unit keeps its identity, but landing never creates an automatic seedling: viability, dormancy, environment and species-specific requirements still affect germination and establishment. The condition map illustrates a typical sexual reproductive pathway, not every instance of apomixis, vegetative reproduction or seedless fruit.

en.misconception: Not every landed seed germinates, and not every pollinated flower produces fruit. A dandelion pappus carries a small fruit; a cherry seed is inside its stone. The comparison cases are not one plant changing species.
en.boundary: The bean is a healthy-seed conditional album, with cold or oxygen limitation represented by pausing later growth. Cherry offers illustrative compatible-success and incompatible-blocked cases, not computed fruit-set probabilities. Dispersal paths and all stage durations are not measurement-calibrated; wind fields and germination rates are not calculated. Cases keep separate state and pause on switching; scrubbing revisits a record rather than reversing plant growth.

narration.label: Suitable starting conditions
narration.text: A bean holds a tiny new plant. Water helps it become active again, but staying underwater is not good: it also needs oxygen. With suitable conditions, a little root usually appears first.
narration.cue: Compare dry, flooded and damp conditions at the bean’s starting state, then restore conditions and observe the root.

narration.label: A seedling does not flower immediately
narration.text: The shoot rises and true leaves unfold. It still needs light, water, nutrients and more growth before it can flower. Next we move to an already mature cherry tree. This is a different comparison case.
narration.cue: Keep the bean’s true-leaf state, note that growth to maturity is not simulated, then switch to cherry with an explicit species change.

narration.label: Arriving pollen is not enough
narration.text: A bee brings pollen to the flower. A compatible pollen tube can keep growing before fertilization may occur. Sometimes pollen arrives without succeeding. When a cherry develops, its seed is hidden inside the stone.
narration.cue: Compare compatible and incompatible cases in the same cherry cutaway, noting the arrested tube and absence of fruit.

narration.label: Ask again after landing
narration.text: Two other plants show different journeys: dandelion fruits ride the wind and burdock hooks catch on animal fur. Reaching a new place does not automatically make a seedling. Ask again: are water, air and temperature suitable here?
narration.cue: Observe wind-borne landing and burdock contact, transport and release. Read the condition map and return to the retained bean comparison.
